[1] repair-manual.pdf p.4
The pump cup is the leather washer on the end of the plunger. When it is dry it will not seal
and the customer reports "the pump does nothing". Oil the pump cup with 3 drops of
Clearburn pump oil every 10 fills; tell the customer this on the return note, because it is the
one piece of maintenance that stops most Northstars coming back.
1. Unscrew the pump cap a quarter turn and withdraw the plunger.
2. Inspect the cup. A cup that is cracked or glazed hard is replaced (part P-CUP2); one
that is merely dry is oiled.
3. Put 3 drops of pump oil on the cup and work it in with your thumb until it is pliable.
4. Refit and pump 10 strokes. The resistance should build by the fourth stroke.
Mantle replacement
Mantles are consumables and are not a warranty item. The Northstar takes two mantles, part
M-21, sold as a 2-pack. A mantle with a hole, a tear or a dark patch is replaced; one that is
simply grey is fine.
1. Remove the globe and brush the old mantle ash off the burner caps with the nylon
brush.
2. Tie the new mantle to the burner cap with the string that comes on it and trim the
string to 10 mm.

[2] faq.md > Can I burn kerosene in the Northstar?
### Can I burn kerosene in the Northstar?

No. The Northstar Dual-Fuel burns Clearburn white gas or unleaded gasoline only. Kerosene or
lamp oil will clog its generator in a single evening and the damage is not covered by warranty.

The Northstar is a pressurized dual-fuel lantern: you pump the tank, light the mantles, and get
the brightest light we sell, bright enough to work under at night. It burns Clearburn white gas,
which is cleaner and keeps the generator clear longer, or regular unleaded gasoline in a pinch. It
must never be run on kerosene or lamp oil, which will clog the generator in a single evening. A
new Northstar should be run outdoors for its first 10 minutes to burn in the mantles. The glass
globe is part G-ND2, and spare mantles are M-21, sold in a 2-pack. The pump, generator and valve
are all serviceable at the Repair Center.

Compatible parts: mantle 2-pack M-21, globe G-ND2, Clearburn White Gas LS-FUEL1, carry case CC-ND2.

[4] repair-manual.pdf p.3
The Northstar is our most repaired product by a wide margin, which is a function of how
many we sell and of how it is used, not of any weakness. Nearly every Northstar fault is one
of four things: a clogged generator, a dry pump cup, a torn mantle, or the wrong fuel. Ask
about the fuel first. The Northstar burns Clearburn white gas or unleaded gasoline. It does
not burn kerosene, and a tank that has had kerosene in it will have a varnished generator
and a sticky check valve. That is a paid repair even inside the warranty period.
Tools for the Northstar bench: 11 mm and 13 mm open-ended wrenches, the generator
wrench (part T-ND2, the thin 9 mm one with the bent handle), a small flat screwdriver, the
pump cup oil bottle, a nylon brush, and the torque driver set to 2.5 N·m for checking.
Generator tube replacement
The generator (part G-GEN2) is the tube that runs up through the burner and carries fuel
from the tank to the mantles. Signs of a bad generator are a weak yellow flame that will not
steady, pulsing light, and a tank that holds pressure but will not deliver it. The part is
$13.00, so a typical generator replacement on a yellow tag comes to $38.00 with the bench
fee.

[5] fuel-safety.md > The fuels we sell
## The fuels we sell

Clearburn White Gas (LS-FUEL1) is sold in 1-quart cans at $12.99. It is a naphtha fuel, highly
refined, with no additives, and it is what the Northstar was designed around. Clearburn Lamp
Oil (LS-OIL1) is sold in 1-quart bottles at $9.99; it is a clear paraffin oil for wick lanterns
and lamps. We do not sell kerosene. K-1 kerosene is available at most hardware stores and some
fuel stations; buy it in a container marked for kerosene, never in a gasoline can.

Shelf life of Clearburn white gas is 5 years in a sealed can and about 1 year once the can has
been opened; write the date you opened it on the can with a marker. Lamp oil keeps indefinitely
if the bottle is closed. Old white gas does not become dangerous, but it gums the generator and
the lantern will burn poorly. If a can has been open for more than a year, dispose of it as
described below and buy fresh.
